test.title: Three Dimensional Geometry - Test 2
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: If the shortest distance between the straight lines <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>λ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>38</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>,</mo></math> then the integral value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi></math> is equal to:

The length of the perpendicular from the point <math><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>4</mn><mo>)</mo></math> on the straight line <math><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mi> </mi></mrow><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> is

Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>.</mo></math> If the mirror image of the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> with respect to the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mn>7</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mn>20</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>|</mo><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>b</mi><mo>|</mo></math> is equal to:

Let $\mathrm{L}_1: \frac{x-1}{2}=\frac{y-2}{3}=\frac{z-3}{4}$ and $\mathrm{L}_2: \frac{x-2}{3}=\frac{y-4}{4}=\frac{z-5}{5}$ be two lines. Then which of the following points lies on the line of the shortest distance between $L_1$ and $L_2$ ?

The lines <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>a</mi><mi>b</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> are coplanar, if:

The lines <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>r</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi>l</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi>r</mi><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced><mo>+</mo><mi>m</mi><mfenced><mrow><mover><mi>i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mover><mi>j</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>-</mo><mover><mi>k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mfenced></math>

question.text: The shortest distance between the lines $\frac{x-3}{2}=\frac{y+15}{-7}=\frac{z-9}{5}$ and $\frac{x+1}{2}=\frac{y-1}{1}=\frac{z-9}{-3}$ is

Then the area (in sq. units) of this triangle, given the point <math><mi>A</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mtext> </mtext><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> is

Let $P$ be the point $(10,-2,-1)$ and $Q$ be the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $R(1,7,6)$ on the line passing through the points $(2,-5,11)$ and $(-6,7,-5)$. Then the length of the line segment $P Q$ is equal to ________

Let the image of the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> in the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi><mo>:</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math>. let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mfenced><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> be a point that divides internally the line segment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mi>Q</mi></math> in the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>3</mn></math>. Then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>22</mn><mfenced><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to

If the shortest distance between the lines  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>-</mo><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>6</mn></msqrt></mrow><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn></math>, then sum of squares of all possible values(s) of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi></math> is
Let the area of the triangle formed by the lines $x+2=y-1=z, \frac{x-3}{5}=\frac{y}{-1}=\frac{z-1}{1}$ and $\frac{x}{-3}=\frac{y-3}{3}=\frac{z-2}{1}$ be $A$. Then $A^2$ is equal to ________

The distance of the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> from the point of intersection of the line joining the points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi><mfenced><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo>-</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and the plane <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo></math> is equal to _____.
